title: Go: SQL Query Builder
description: Build a type-safe SQL query builder in Go with method chaining, parameterized placeholders, JOINs, aggregations, subqueries, and INSERT/UPDATE support.

steps.title: Query struct and parameter tracking
steps.description: Define a `Query` struct with `sql strings.Builder` and `args []interface{}`. Implement `addArg(v interface{})` that appends a `$N` placeholder and stores the value. Write `String()` method returning the built SQL and args. Build a simple SELECT and print the SQL with placeholders.
hints: Use `strings.Builder` for efficient SQL string concatenation
Track arg index with a counter and append `fmt.Sprintf("$%d", idx)` as placeholder

verification.successMessage: Query struct correctly builds SQL with parameterized placeholders!
verification.failureMessage: Print the SQL string with placeholders and the args slice.

steps.title: SELECT, FROM, WHERE method chaining
steps.description: Implement `Select(columns ...string)`, `From(table string)`, and `Where(condition string, args ...interface{})` as chainable methods returning `*Query`. Build `Select("name", "age").From("users").Where("age > $1", 18)` and print the generated SQL and args.
hints: Each method modifies the Query and returns `q` for chaining
`Select` appends to SELECT clause, `From` adds FROM, `Where` adds WHERE with AND joining
Handle multiple Where calls by joining with AND

verification.test: output.includes('SELECT name, age FROM users WHERE') && output.includes('$1')
verification.successMessage: Method chaining builds valid SELECT ... FROM ... WHERE SQL!
verification.failureMessage: Print the generated SQL showing SELECT, FROM, and WHERE clauses.

steps.title: JOIN support
steps.description: Implement `Join(table, condition string)`, `LeftJoin(table, condition string)`, and `RightJoin(table, condition string)` methods. Build a query joining `users` with `orders`: `Select("u.name", "o.total").From("users u").Join("orders o", "o.user_id = u.id")`. Print the result.
hints: Store JOIN clauses in a `[]join` slice where each has type, table, and condition
In `String()`, append JOIN clauses after the FROM clause
Print the JOIN clause: `fmt.Printf("JOIN type: %s\n", join.clause)`

verification.successMessage: JOIN methods correctly append INNER, LEFT, and RIGHT JOIN clauses!
verification.failureMessage: Print the generated SQL showing JOIN and ON clauses.

steps.title: Aggregation with GROUP BY and HAVING
steps.description: Implement `GroupBy(columns ...string)` and `Having(condition string, args ...interface{})` methods. Build a query that selects department aggregate: `Select("dept", "COUNT(*) as count").From("employees").GroupBy("dept").Having("COUNT(*) > $1", 5)`. Print the SQL.
hints: GROUP BY clause goes after WHERE and before ORDER BY
HAVING is similar to WHERE but uses aggregate conditions after GROUP BY
Support `OrderBy(columns ...string)` and `Limit(offset, count int)` as well

verification.successMessage: GROUP BY and HAVING correctly build aggregation queries!
verification.failureMessage: Print the SQL showing GROUP BY, HAVING, and aggregate functions.

steps.title: Subqueries
steps.description: Implement a `SubQuery(q *Query, alias string)` function that wraps a Query as a subquery expression. Support subqueries in FROM (as derived tables) and WHERE (with IN and EXISTS). Build a query: `Select("*").From(SubQuery(inner, "t")).Where("id IN $1", SubQuery(sub, ""))`. Print the parenthesized SQL.
hints: SubQuery wraps the inner SQL in parentheses: `(%s)`
For FROM subqueries, append an alias: `(%s) AS %s`
For WHERE subqueries with IN, use: `IN (%s)` with proper placeholder integration

verification.successMessage: Subqueries are correctly wrapped in parentheses with proper aliasing!
verification.failureMessage: Print the generated SQL showing nested SELECT in parentheses.

steps.title: INSERT and UPDATE builders
steps.description: Implement `InsertInto(table string, columns ...string) *Query` with `Values(values ...interface{})`, and `Update(table string) *Query` with `Set(column string, value interface{})` and `Where`. Build and print INSERT INTO users (name, age) VALUES ($1, $2) and UPDATE users SET name = $1 WHERE id = $2.
hints: INSERT builds `INSERT INTO table (col1, col2) VALUES ($1, $2)` from columns and values
UPDATE builds `UPDATE table SET col1 = $1, col2 = $2 WHERE ...`
Each Set call adds a column = placeholder pair, separated by comma

verification.successMessage: INSERT and UPDATE builders generate correct DML SQL with placeholders!
verification.failureMessage: Print both INSERT and UPDATE SQL statements with placeholders.
